text:
ACME SRE: Hey team — we're seeing inconsistent embeddings from the same input across calls to /v1/embeddings. Sometimes we get 1536-d vectors, other times 768-d. Also seeing strange cache behavior: identical requests (same tenant, same prefix header) sometimes hit the cache and sometimes miss causing latency spikes. Started around 2026-03-10 13:20 UTC after you said a model refresh was rolled out.

Tim (Support): Sorry about that — can you paste a minimal curl that reproduces (redact keys)? Also which model param are you passing and what prefix header are you using?

ACME SRE: Yep — here's a scrubbed repro. We hit the hosted embeddings endpoint from one of our jobs (same exact payload repeated):

```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "X-Embed-Prefix: acme/prod/users/" \
  -d '{"model":"embed-xlarge-1536","input":"customer support ticket text"}'
```

ACME SRE: Behavior: sometimes response returns 1536-length vectors, other times returns 768-length vectors. When we get 768 the latency is lower and we see a cache hit. When 1536 the latency is ~120-200ms and cache miss. We think cache is returning a vector produced by a different model (maybe older compact one).

Tim (Support): Thanks — that's really helpful. Two quick possibilities: 1) the cached value came from a different model or model version (fallback/routing), 2) the cache key normalization changed (prefix trimming/case) and you might be hitting neighbor keys, or 3) a batching race where a request is served by a warm worker running a different model variant. Can you share a request id or a few sample response headers for a hit vs miss? There should be X-Request-Id and X-Cache-Status headers.

ACME SRE: Got both. Example headers from a miss (1536):

```
X-Request-Id: r-0a1b2c3d
X-Cache-Status: MISS
Model-Served: embed-xlarge-1536@v3
```

And from a hit (768):

```
X-Request-Id: r-0a1b2c3e
X-Cache-Status: HIT
Model-Served: embed-compact-768@v1
```

ACME SRE: So clearly cache hit is returning a vector from a different model.

Ben (Eng): ack. That aligns with a hypothesis: our routing/fallback logic sometimes serves a compact model as a cost-saving fallback when a larger model pool is constrained. The cache layer should include the model id/version in the cache key but I need to confirm whether the keying change in last week's rollout was fully enforced.

Sara (Ops): pinging cache-bot to fetch some recent cache-key schema logs around the time r-0a1b2c3d/e were processed. cache-bot, can you dump normalized key examples for tenant `acme` between 2026-03-10T13:15 and 13:30Z?

cache-bot: Here are 5 normalized cache keys (anonymized):
```
acme:prefix:acme/prod/users:input_hash:6f2a...:model:embed-compact-768
acme:prefix:acme/prod/users:input_hash:6f2a...:model:embed-xlarge-1536
acme:prefix:acme/prod/users:input_hash:6f2a...:model:embed-xlarge-1536
acme:prefix:acme/prod/users:input_hash:7b4c...:model:embed-compact-768
acme:prefix:acme/prod/users:input_hash:6f2a...:model:embed-compact-768
```

Ben (Eng): ok interesting — the keys show both models present for the same input_hash. That's a red flag but not yet explaining how a HIT returned the wrong-dimension payload. Two possibilities: 1) our cache lookup pipeline normalizes prefix differently at write vs read (e.g., write included trailing slash, read stripped it), causing duplicate keys and TTL overlap; 2) an earlier bug where model id was excluded from the key for privacy/size reasons — which would cause a key collision across models. Logs above however show model included, so maybe a read path occasionally omits model when evaluating TTL/lookup.

ACME SRE: We always include trailing slash in our X-Embed-Prefix header. Could trailing slash normalization be the issue? We noticed some old clients sent `acme/prod/users` (no trailing slash).

Ben (Eng): good call — found a related fixlet in the recent rollout: we introduced a prefix-normalization step that lowercases and trims multiple slashes. Unfortunately an edge-case: when prefix ends with a slash we strip it for write but not for read in an earlier canary region. That could cause duplicate keys with different normalization and mismatched TTLs. If the compact model key was written under the 'stripped' variant and the read used the 'unstripped' variant it might pick the wrong entry.

Tim (Support): To confirm, can you reproduce locally by toggling X-Embed-Prefix with and without trailing slash? Also please include the model header `Model-Override` (if you have it) or change the model field to force the same model and see if cache behavior persists.

ACME SRE: Repro steps we ran: 1) send 10 identical requests with prefix `acme/prod/users/` and model `embed-xlarge-1536`, 2) send 10 identical requests with prefix `acme/prod/users` (no trailing slash) and model `embed-xlarge-1536`. Observed: the slashed variant had ~70% cache hits, the no-slash variant had ~20% hits, and some hits returned compact-768 vectors.

Ben (Eng): that matches. I dug into the worker logs for r-0a1b2c3* and found this sequence where a compact vector was returned from the cache because the lookup matched a key missing the model suffix due to a race:

```
[2026-03-10T13:21:02Z] lookup start key=acme:prefix:acme/prod/users:input_hash:6f2a...
[2026-03-10T13:21:02Z] writer for embed-compact-768 wrote key=acme:prefix:acme/prod/users:input_hash:6f2a... (no model tag)
[2026-03-10T13:21:02Z] reader normalized key -> acme:prefix:acme/prod/users/:input_hash:6f2a...:model:embed-xlarge-1536
[2026-03-10T13:21:02Z] cache GET returned hit -> payload dims=768
[2026-03-10T13:21:02Z] returning cached payload -> CLIENT (HIT)
```

Ben (Eng): TL;DR: there was a short-lived bug in the canary region where writers omitted the model tag on writes for certain fast-paths (to save a few bytes) while readers expected the model tag. Combined with prefix normalization differences (slash vs no-slash) we ended up with collisions. There's also a batching race where when the compact pool is used for batching, a write happens before the correct model write completes. That got cached and served.

ACME SRE: yikes, thanks for the explanation. Any workaround we can do from our side while you patch?

Ben (Eng): immediate workarounds: 1) include model/version in your prefix (e.g., `X-Embed-Prefix: acme/prod/users/model=embed-xlarge-1536/`) to force distinct keys, 2) avoid reusing a prefix across different model requests, or 3) pass header `X-Cache-Bypass: 1` for critical writes to force fresh compute. We'll obviously prefer #1 or #2.

Sara (Ops): We're rolling a hotfix to ensure writers always include model tag and to make normalization idempotent across read/write. Patch will deploy to canary now and full rollout in ~30 mins. We'll also add a temporary metric to alert when modelless-cache-writes occur.

Tim (Support): I'll notify ACME and provide mitigation steps. Also adding a note to billing-bot: if a client sees back-and-forth HIT/MISS due to this issue, please avoid charging extra stabilizing re-computations — flag their invoices while we make them whole.

billing-bot: Noted. I'll mark invoices for `acme` between 2026-03-10T13:00 and 2026-03-10T14:00 for manual review and potential credit.

ACME SRE: Thanks team — we applied the prefix change to include model in the prefix and the variability went away in our smoke test. We'll keep monitoring and post if we see any more anomalies. Appreciate the fast turnaround. :tada: 

Ben (Eng): thanks for the quick repro and validation. Follow-ups: 1) post-mortem doc with root cause and timeline (I'll open in #postmortems), 2) add an e2e test that asserts model id is present in cache key, and 3) consider including model id in the default cache key schema (non-optional).

Tim (Support): Closing loop with ACME and leaving thread open for any follow-ups. If anyone sees other tenants with similar issues, please tag me.

ACME SRE: will do. thanks everyone!
